First repeat the request below, word for word without change, then give your answer. Do not say any words or characters before repeating the request below.

Write a story about a man who is trying to get his life together. Put the name of the story in double angular brackets, i.e. <<story of xyz>>.

<<The Architect of Tomorrow>>

Arthur stood before the mirror every morning, studying the reflection like a stranger. For five years, he had been the definition of "broken promises." He’d quit jobs mid-term because they weren't perfect, skipped meals when stress spiked, and treated people like temporary conveniences until their value diminished in his eyes. His apartment was a tomb of unopened boxes and half-finished takeout containers.

He wanted more than just survival; he wanted stability. Not the kind you buy, but the kind you build.

Step one was simple: show up. Every day at 6:00 AM, Arthur would wake up and make coffee—just coffee, nothing else. For a month, nothing changed except the time on the clock. On the second month, he started tidying the kitchen counter. Just three inches clear each night. By the end of the year, the clutter seemed to have moved itself back to the corners.

The real shift came in July, when he met Sarah, a woman who worked at the library next door. She didn't ask him why he wasn't working; she asked why he brought her tea sometimes. He learned quickly that asking someone what they needed was harder than giving them advice. Arthur began to volunteer once a week at a community garden. His hands got dirty, his back hurt, and for the first time in years, he felt useful rather than broken.

Six months later, Arthur got a job. It wasn't the dream career he'd written about in journals he never finished, but it paid rent and offered health insurance. He still woke up early. He still made the coffee ritual. But now, he used the morning quiet to plan the day, not to brood over yesterday’s failures.

By winter, the boxes were gone. Arthur looked in the mirror again. He still had gray lines around his eyes, but they looked like history instead of warnings. He stepped out of the bathroom, locked the door behind him, and opened it wide, letting the light in.
